NEPTUNUS Phase 3 program: ianalumab 300 mg subcutaneous monthly (the book's related asset row is 'ianalumab s.c. q4w'); open-label extension NCT05985915
lookup.py demand Benlysta: CMS Medicare Part D 2024 (Benlysta*), $216,806,703.67 over 5,831 beneficiaries = $37,182 per beneficiary
column12: Judgement: house convention. Benlysta is the closest marketed comparator. It is the only approved BAFF-pathway drug, used in the same rheumatology practices, and its subcutaneous form is self-injected like ianalumab. No drug is approved for Sjogren's itself. Part B IV Benlysta was $34,064 per beneficiary in 2024. The case against: a first-in-disease drug with Breakthrough status may be priced above an older biologic. And per-beneficiary spend understates a full year, because starters and stoppers fill only part of it

column11: Bell CF et al., Lupus Science & Medicine 2020;7(1):e000357 (MarketScan, 1,879 US patients starting IV belimumab 2011-2015): 26.2% discontinued within six months; at a constant rate that is 1-(1-0.262)^2 = 45.5% a year. The dazukibart seed already carries this figure
column12: Reuses the book's measured belimumab persistence, since belimumab is the same mechanism class in rheumatology. The case against: in NEPTUNUS ianalumab showed adverse events similar to placebo, and monthly subcutaneous dosing may persist better than IV infusion. Its modest effect on ESSDAI (about 1 to 1.3 points over placebo) may push the other way

column12: The BLA was submitted in Q1 2026 under priority review, which is a 6-month review after the 60-day filing period, about 8 months from submission. SLE (NCT05624749, primary completion 2027-04-12) would launch later; Novartis moved its SLE submission forward to 2027 (Q2 2026 6-K)

column11: Rosas J et al., Rheumatol Int 2019;39(6):991-9, doi:10.1007/s00296-019-04285-w (PMID 30891620), SJOGRENSER registry, 437 patients: ESSDAI moderate (5-13) in 15% and high (14 or more) in 5%, so 20% have ESSDAI of 5 or more, the systemic-activity threshold the NEPTUNUS trials enrolled on
column12: Judgement that the label will follow trial entry (active systemic disease). The case for lower: the registry itself says its cohort has less activity than other European cohorts, and NEPTUNUS also required seropositivity (about 75% anti-SSA positive in Maciel 2017), which is not applied here. The case for higher: a prospective longitudinal cohort reports 59% with ESSDAI under 5, so 41% at 5 or more (PMC11759214, search summary, not opened), and a label may be broader than trial entry

column10: share of the eligible untreated pool per year
column11: Anchor: 28% of US patients with moderate to severe SLE were on belimumab in 2022, 37% in 2023 (Spherix real-world audit, reported by Healio 2024-04-25, 'Biologic use in moderate to severe lupus rose 45% since 2021', https://www.healio.com/news/rheumatology/20240425/exciting-time-biologic-use-in-moderate-to-severe-lupus-rose-45-since-2021). Solved at steady state: holding 28% on therapy against 45.54% annual discontinuation needs 0.4554 x 0.28 = 12.75% of the pool starting each year, which is 12.75/72 = 17.71% of the 72% untreated
column12: Judgement: the multiple is 1.0. Belimumab was the first targeted therapy in SLE, as ianalumab would be in Sjogren's, and 2022 is its 11th year. The case for lower: ianalumab's effect over placebo is small, and competitors (dazodalibep, nipocalimab, telitacicept, efgartigimod) have Sjogren's Phase 3s running. The case for higher: the 2023 figure is 37%. Run through the engine (forecast.py, carryover 1, Zeposia curve), the stock reaches 26% of the eligible pool in year 5 and 30% in year 7, then drifts to 18% by year 15, because the engine drops stoppers from the pool. The healio figures came from a search summary, so the second reader should confirm them
